svg.text: The article runs as a single chain of argument, each stage building on the last — from the failure of fixed-neuron
models, through oscillations and ephaptic coupling, to a full wave-based theory of cognition and consciousness —
with the two densest stages (spatial computing and traveling-wave analog computation) opening into their own…

g.text: A chain: classical models fail to explain flexible cognition, which motivates oscillations and ephaptic coupling, which
motivate Spatial Computing theory, which motivates traveling-wave analog computation, which together explain anesthesia
and ground a new theory of consciousness.

g.title: Fixed-function neuron models can't explain flexible cognition — Connectionist models assume each neuron has one stable job, but many prefrontal neurons multiplex several kinds of information. — → spya-k046f6
Neurons show mixed selectivity: one cell, many roles — Context-dependent, nonlinear responses let a small population do much more computational work, but require dynamic routing. — → spya-v0gbwq

g.text: Inside: Traveling Waves and Analog Computation
A chain: evidence that waves travel and shift coding states leads into the claim that this travel is itself a form of
computation, efficient and applicable to combining contexts.
